quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 operating earnings of $1.36 per share, or $742 million, versus $1.43 a year earlier — CFO Trevor Mihalik attributes the decline to timing items (the 2025 Transmission Holdco minority-interest sale and income-tax timing expected to reverse by year end), not underlying performance. Year-to-date operating earnings $3.01 per share versus $2.98. On the strength of the first half AEP RAISED 2026 operating earnings guidance to $6.25 to $6.55 per share from $6.15 to $6.45, reaffirmed its 7% to 9% annual growth rate and an operating EPS CAGR of greater than 9% through 2030 supported by the $78 billion capital plan. Regulated earned ROE was 9.2% for the quarter, with a stated path to 9.5% by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 operating EPS $1.36 ($742 million) vs $1.43; YTD $3.01 vs $2.98; FY2026 guidance raised to $6.25-$6.55 from $6.15-$6.45

quarterly_data.signal: CONTRACTED LOAD ADDITIONS REACH 69 GIGAWATTS through 2030, up six gigawatts from the 63 GW disclosed last quarter — 'AEP contracted an additional six gigawatts of load, primarily driven by fully executed LOAs in Texas.' All of it is supported by fully executed ESAs and LOAs that require customers to secure land, complete interconnection studies, provide detailed load forecasts and fund the associated infrastructure investments. Geographic split: Texas 45 GW, Ohio 12 GW, and Oklahoma, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana and Virginia combined 12 GW. Management stresses counterparty quality — 'the vast majority of these projects are being advanced by well-capitalized hyperscalers and large industrial customers with significant financial resources.' Executed LOAs and ESAs have increased every quarter for the last six to seven quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: 69 GW contracted load through 2030 (up 6 GW from 63 GW last quarter); Texas 45 GW, Ohio 12 GW, other states 12 GW

quarterly_data.signal: AEP TEXAS SUBMITTED 45 GIGAWATTS OF PROJECTS INTO ERCOT'S BATCH ZERO process, forecast between now and 2032, with ERCOT expected to determine eligibility on August 7. The credit support is already in hand: 'just over the past month, we have collected nearly $2 billion in cash or collateral for load commitments in ERCOT, which represents all the required credit support for the full 45 gigawatts included in AEP Texas's Batch Zero filing.' Of the 205 gigawatts ERCOT published as eligible for Batch Zero, AEP is 'roughly, call it, a quarter of that', and the CFO treats its 45 GW as firm — a worst case only slips projects from Batch Zero to Batch One. Critical for the equipment chain: the $78 billion capital plan assumed only about 13 gigawatts of interconnection in Texas and 'does not anticipate this magnitude of load growth', and there is 'almost 100 gigawatts in Texas behind that 45 gigawatts', with 195 gigawatts of parties actively trying to interconnect to the queue.
quarterly_data.figure: 45 GW submitted to ERCOT Batch Zero (out of 205 GW eligible); nearly $2 billion of cash/collateral posted; $78B plan assumed only about 13 GW of Texas interconnection; almost 100 GW more queued behind it; 195 GW in the interconnection queue

quarterly_data.signal: FIVE-YEAR CAPITAL PLAN OF $78 BILLION for 2026 through 2030, expected to result in nearly 11% rate base CAGR — 'AEP's five-year capital plan stood at just $38 billion only four years ago.' Beyond the base plan the company has 'line of sight to over $10 billion of incremental investments that are not included in the $78 billion, consisting of the fuel cells for the Wyoming project, the Piketon transmission opportunity, and incremental power generation.' A new 2027 to 2031 plan will be introduced on the third-quarter earnings call, with the secured generation investments expected to be an important driver of the long-term growth outlook. Financing for the base plan is de-risked: a $3 billion marketed equity transaction settled under forward contracts by May 2028 addresses all anticipated marketed equity needs, with a targeted FFO to debt ratio of 14% to 15%.
quarterly_data.figure: $78B five-year capital plan 2026-2030 (nearly 11% rate base CAGR), up from $38B four years ago; over $10B of identified incremental investment outside the plan

quarterly_data.signal: TURBINE SUPPLY IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND AEP IS PRE-BUYING IT: an additional three gigawatts of gas-fired turbines secured during the quarter takes total secured turbine capacity to approximately 13 gigawatts for deployment through 2031, and AEP is 'leveraging our sizable market position and strategic manufacturer relationships to secure up to 10 gigawatts of incremental turbine capacity through 2035' — an option it is not committed to. CEO Bill Fehrman named the suppliers: 'using our size and scale and our relationships with namely GE Vernova and Mitsubishi to get this equipment locked up... we know that generation is going to be a driving force, and because of that, it's a scarce resource and will become increasingly more valuable.' Roughly half of the 13 GW already sits in the $78 billion plan; the other half rolls into the 2027-2031 plan. The 10 GW option is timed to replace aging coal and gas plants as they retire.
quarterly_data.figure: Three gigawatts of turbines added in the quarter, taking total secured turbine capacity to approximately 13 GW through 2031; option on up to 10 GW more through 2035; about half of the 13 GW already inside the $78B plan

quarterly_data.signal: TWO PROJECTS BEYOND THE BASE PLAN ARE MOVING TO DEFINITIVE AGREEMENTS AHEAD OF THE THIRD-QUARTER CAPITAL-PLAN REFRESH. Piketon (Ohio) transmission: AEP is 'working towards definitive agreements with the prospective offtaker, SP Energy', anticipates executed documents in the third quarter and would then roll the project into the 2027-2031 five-year plan; the company frames it as showcasing 'our industry-leading expertise in developing and operating 765 kV transmission infrastructure.' Wyoming fuel cells: at the contractual June 30 deadline AEP amended the agreement with the unnamed hyperscaler offtaker, modifying key protection terms so AEP is 'adequately compensated for their requested timing accommodations' while keeping the original December 2026 milestone intact, after which the hyperscaler may deploy the fuel cells at an alternate location if the Cheyenne, Wyoming site does not advance. Timing is gating: the fuel cells 'need to be installed and ready to go by the end of 2028 to qualify for the investment tax credit.'
quarterly_data.figure: Piketon definitive agreements targeted for the third quarter with offtaker SP Energy; Wyoming fuel-cell December 2026 milestone intact, units must be installed by the end of 2028 to qualify for the investment tax credit
quarterly_data.counterparty: SP Energy (Piketon transmission offtaker); unnamed hyperscaler (Wyoming fuel cells)

quarterly_data.signal: LARGE-LOAD TARIFF FRAMEWORK NOW COVERS FIVE JURISDICTIONS — Virginia approved AEP's proposed large load tariff in June, 'bringing the total number of approved tariffs across the portfolio to five', with three additional filings pending. The tariffs 'require customers to make long-term commitments and support the investments necessary to serve their demand' and provide protections against project delays and changing development timelines. Because new large load signs take-or-pay electric service agreements, AEP projects fixed cost offsets for residential customers of up to $16 billion at its vertically integrated utilities — already flowing through as base rate reductions (an Ohio order received; Indiana Michigan Power to file a base rate decrease later this summer).
quarterly_data.figure: Five large-load tariffs approved and three more filings pending; up to $16 billion of projected fixed-cost offsets for residential customers

quarterly_data.signal: GENERATION ADDITIONS TO SERVE THE LOAD: Public Service Company of Oklahoma received a separate order in May approving its request to procure 1.3 gigawatts of generation resources; AEP has announced one West Virginia project of about 1.2 gigawatts with 'a number of other projects that are heading down the pathway' toward the governor's 50 by 50 target; and it is evaluating a GenCo structure alongside an early-stage nuclear strategy 'driven by demand from potential customers who value alternative forms of long-term baseload generation to support their rapidly growing demand', on fee-based arrangements with robust capital protection measures. AEP also buys existing generation into rate base for its vertically integrated utilities (projects purchased for Indiana Michigan Power) and offers behind-the-meter bridging power so customers get immediate capacity while transmission and generation are built.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.3 GW of generation procurement approved for Public Service Company of Oklahoma; about 1.2 GW project announced in West Virginia
